pathway.title: PITNEY BOWES INC /DE/ — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is average and weakening: two segments that both depend on the postal system earn a high margin on a base that is shrinking. Total revenue fell 6.61% in 2025 and 2.11% in the first nine months of 2026, and the shrinkage is steady rather than sudden. SendTech earns an adjusted EBIT margin of 37.84%, with services at 45.48% of its revenue and USD 624.43 million of contracted future performance obligations, but 38.22% of its revenue is lease and financing income from a shrinking book, and Presort lost 5.94 percentage points of margin and 26.19% of adjusted EBIT on a 4.18% revenue fall, an operating leverage of 6.27x. A decline in mail volumes therefore cuts earnings faster than revenue in the segment that has a fixed processing and transport network. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F10; calculation F13; calculation F15; calculation F19.

Cash generation is real but flattered, so creditors should size debt service on operating cash flow before the finance receivable release. Operating cash flow over the last twelve months was USD 569.91 million, 114.51% of EBITDA (Reported), but without USD 100.00 million released from a shrinking finance receivable book it was 94.42%, and 79.49% of the USD 186.66 million nine-month rise came from a smaller outflow on payables and accruals. Operating cash flow before the release, less capital expenditures of USD 65.29 million, was USD 404.62 million, inside the range of the issuer's 2026 adjusted free cash flow guidance, USD 380 million to USD 420 million, which is defined differently. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 67; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F06; calculation F08; calculation F09.

Leverage has improved by 0.52x since year-end 2025 but not on a growing earnings base, so further gains depend on cash that the board can redirect. Net debt to EBITDA (Reported) fell from 3.77x at year-end 2025 to 3.25x at 2026-09-30, or 3.27x pro forma for the USD 11 million of repurchases to October 23, 2026; the effect of the dividend payable on December 8, 2026 is not established because its total is not stated, and pro forma cash is not established. Of the fall, 0.32x came from higher EBITDA and 0.20x from lower net debt, but the EBITDA gain follows losses of USD 45.68 million on foreign exchange and debt activities in nine months 2025 and gains of USD 8.77 million in 2026, and last-twelve-month EBITDA has slipped from USD 503.26 million at 2026-06-30 to USD 497.69 million. The issuer's adjusted EBITDA rose 4.49% to USD 432.41 million in nine months only because USD 23.13 million of pension expense is excluded from 2026 and not from 2025; on the 2025 definition it fell 1.10%. EBITDA covered cash interest 3.65x, and a 10% fall in EBITDA at constant net debt would lift net leverage to 3.61x, a 20% fall to 4.07x. The computed 3.25x sits below the 4.75x total net leverage covenant level for 2026 but is not covenant headroom, because the agreement's definitions are not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 9; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F01; calculation F02; calculation F12; calculation F16; calculation F20.

Liquidity is adequate for the next two years but the maturity wall is concentrated and conditional, so refinancing is the central test after 2028. Cash plus remaining revolver capacity was USD 695.51 million at 2026-09-30 against a current portion of debt of USD 24.73 million (pro forma liquidity is not established), yet 82.59% of principal matures between 2029 and 2032 and two springing tests accelerate the 2031 term loan and the revolver if liquidity is below the redemption amount of the 2029 notes plus USD 100 million, a test amount of USD 576.00 million, before December 14, 2028, with a matching test of USD 330.00 million for the convertible notes before May 16, 2030. The liquidity definition sits in an agreement that is not supplied, so headroom is not calculable. Term loans are 45.79% of principal at floating rates, so a 100 bp move changes annual interest by USD 8.78 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F03; calculation F04; calculation F05.

Financial policy is the swing factor because shareholder returns, not debt service, set the pace of deleveraging. Returns of USD 387.07 million over the last twelve months were 95.66% of operating cash flow less capital expenditures before the release, and in 2025 returns of USD 429.42 million exceeded operating cash flow of USD 383.26 million; in the first nine months of 2026 returns were 2.29x the USD 107.78 million of debt principal repaid, with USD 165.91 million of repurchase authorisation left. The board can cut returns at any time and the covenants cap leverage, but the baskets that limit distributions are not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F07; calculation F14.

Claims outside the debt figures and missing documents limit confidence more than any single ratio. Customer deposits at the Pitney Bowes Bank were USD 647.95 million at 2026-09-30 and the issuer names depositor withdrawals as a liquidity risk, a claim larger than cash, the Kingsbridge and Trilogy suit seeks more than USD 100 million with no accrual stated, and the pension buy-out is not costed. Debt and cash are reported for the whole group, so industrial leverage and the finance book's matched funding cannot be separated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F15.

The primary downside is faster erosion of the mail base while the finance book stops releasing cash and buybacks continue, and its first visible sign would be a Presort quarter with less volume than the second quarter of 2026 or a falling receivable release. The guidance implies fourth-quarter adjusted EBIT of USD 89.65 million to USD 109.65 million, 3.74% to 21.30% below the third quarter, and adjusted free cash flow of USD 41.24 million to USD 81.24 million, so the guidance implies that part of the third-quarter cash benefit, which the issuer attributes to new client prepayments after a competitor's exit, does not repeat. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_q22026earningspressrelea.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation F11.

runs.text: A contracted, high-margin SendTech base supports debt service, because SendTech future performance obligations are USD 624.43 million, services are 45.48% of its revenue and its adjusted EBIT margin is 37.84%, so a large part of cash flow is visible several quarters ahead and survives a weak equipment year, although 38.22% of its revenue is lease and financing income from a shrinking book. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F15; calculation F19.

Scale in a regulated niche supports Presort cash flow, because the issuer describes itself as the largest USPS workshare partner with a national processing network and volume grew 4% in the third quarter, so scale supports volume retention and client wins, although the same dependence on the postal service is also the main risk. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A).

Falling leverage and rising cover support creditors, because net debt to EBITDA (Reported) fell to 3.25x, or 3.27x pro forma for the October repurchases with the dividend effect not established, and cover rose to 3.65x, so the issuer could absorb a 10% EBITDA fall and still sit at 3.61x on this measure. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F01; calculation F02; calculation F12.

Refinanced liquidity and a late first maturity support the near term, because cash plus remaining revolver capacity is USD 695.51 million, pro forma liquidity is not established, no final maturity falls before March 2029 and the margin on the 2032 term loan was cut by 75 bp, so refinancing risk does not arise before the springing-test date in December 2028. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 1; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F03.

Low capital intensity and completed restructuring support conversion, because capital expenditures are 3.51% of revenue and the 2025 plan that removed about 550 positions finished in the second quarter of 2026, so a large share of EBITDA reaches cash before interest and returns. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation F10.

Structural decline of the mail base constrains creditors, because the meter population and the mailing install base are eroding, Presort volume fell in the first half of 2026 before growing 4% in the third quarter, total revenue fell 6.61% in 2025 and Presort adjusted EBIT fell 26.19% on a 4.18% revenue fall, so earnings are exposed to operating leverage that a lender cannot hedge. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F10; calculation F13.

Cash flow quality constrains creditors, because operating cash flow of USD 569.91 million includes USD 100.00 million released from finance receivables and a payables swing worth 79.49% of the nine-month rise, so the surplus over EBITDA is not a recurring cushion. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F06; calculation F09.

Shareholder returns constrain deleveraging, because buybacks and dividends took 95.66% of cash flow before the release over the last twelve months and exceeded operating cash flow less capital expenditures in 2025, so the board, not the lenders, decides how fast debt falls. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F07; calculation F14.

Maturity concentration and conditionality constrain refinancing, because 82.59% of principal matures from 2029 to 2032, two springing tests tie the 2031 term loan and the revolver to liquidity, and floating-rate term loans are 45.79% of principal against 37% a year earlier, so a weak 2028 would narrow the refinancing window and raise interest cost. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F04; calculation F05.

Claims outside debt and missing documents constrain confidence, because Bank deposits of USD 647.95 million, a lawsuit seeking more than USD 100 million without a stated accrual and an uncosted pension buy-out sit outside the debt figures, and the executed credit agreement and the proxy statement are not supplied, so headroom and governance cannot be verified. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation F15; calculation F16.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No material acquisition, sponsor buyout or change of control appears in the documents supplied; a USD 2.2 million acquisition in the first quarter of 2025 is the only one in the cash flow statements and is not described. The transactions that matter to creditors are the August 2024 ecommerce exit, the 2025 refinancing and convertible issue, and the 2026 note add-on, term loan extension and tender offer. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 85.

In August 2024 the issuer sold 81% of the voting interests of its ecommerce logistics subsidiary to an affiliate of Hilco Commercial Industrial for de minimis consideration and kept 19% of the votes and all of the economic interest; the subsidiary then filed for Chapter 11 and its liquidation plan was confirmed on November 25, 2024. The issuer funded USD 28 million of debtor-in-possession financing, USD 20 million has been repaid and USD 8.00 million is fully reserved. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 85; calculation A17.

In the first quarter of 2025 the issuer redeemed the remaining notes due March 2028 at a loss of USD 17 million and signed a new senior secured credit agreement with a revolver of USD 265 million (later USD 400 million), a USD 160 million term loan due 2028 and a USD 615 million term loan due 2032, recording a further loss of USD 8 million on the refinancing. In August 2025 it issued USD 230 million of 1.50% convertible senior notes due 2030 whose net proceeds of USD 221 million paid for a capped call (premium USD 24.70 million), share repurchases and general purposes, in amounts the sources do not split. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22.

In 2026 the issuer added USD 150 million to its notes due March 2029, raised the revolver from USD 400 million to USD 450 million, borrowed USD 150 million more under its term loan and extended that loan to May 2031 to repay the notes due March 2027, tendered USD 46 million of its notes due 2037 and 2043 at a discount for a gain of USD 5 million, and cut the margin on the 2032 term loan by 75 bp. No final maturity now falls before March 2029, but the term loan due 2031 and the revolver accelerate if liquidity is below the cost of redeeming the 2029 notes plus USD 100 million before December 14, 2028, with a matching test for the convertible notes before May 16, 2030. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 1.

After the 2026-09-30 balance sheet date the issuer repurchased shares for USD 11 million between October 1 and October 23, 2026, paid USD 66 million of pension lump sums from plan assets in October 2026 and the board approved a quarterly dividend of USD 0.10 per share payable on December 8, 2026. These subsequent events are kept out of the period figures. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 1.

fields.value: Four limitations decide how far the analysis can be pushed. The annual report supplied is the original Form 10-K, while every 2026 filing and release cites a Form 10-K/A for the same year that is not in the set. No supplied document publishes company-level adjusted earnings or adjusted free cash flow for full-year 2025, and the 2026 adjusted measures exclude pension expense that prior periods still carry. Debt, cash and capital spending are reported for the consolidated group only, with no finance-versus-industrial split. Credit ratings and market quotes were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PITNEY BOWES INC /DE/ (issuer id pbi), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit snapshot. Scope: Financial foundation, the statements, debt, net debt and credit ratios built from the seven supplied filings and releases, with the post-balance-sheet events to the cutoff.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage on reported EBITDA fell to 3.25x at September 30, 2026 from 3.77x at year-end 2025, and EBITDA covered cash interest 3.65x, so creditors have moderate headroom that depends on continued debt paydown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C61; calculation C52; calculation C62.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow funded the paydown but also had to carry USD 246.32 million of buybacks and dividends in the first nine months, 70.74% of operating cash flow, so a pause in returns or a weaker cash year would stall deleveraging. Adjusted-EBITDA leverage cannot be stated because no supplied document gives the issuer's full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage peaked at 4.44x total debt to LTM reported EBITDA at March 31, 2026, when the 2029 notes had been increased but the 2027 notes were still outstanding, and fell to 3.79x by September 30, 2026 after a term loan upsizing repaid the 2027 notes and a tender retired part of the 2037 and 2043 notes. The fall is debt, not earnings: LTM reported EBITDA slipped from USD 503.26 million at June 30, 2026 to USD 497.69 million at September 30, 2026, because third-quarter reported EBITDA of USD 127.28 million was below the USD 132.85 million of a year earlier and pension non-service cost was USD 8.63 million higher, so further deleveraging depends on cash paydown rather than EBITDA growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C54; calculation C60; calculation C21; calculation C22.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cover improved from 3.19x in FY2025 to 3.65x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026 as cash interest paid fell and EBITDA rose, and the cut of 0.75 percentage points in the margin on the 2032 term loan lowers the run-rate further. Both EBITDA and cash interest are consolidated, so the cover blends the finance and industrial perimeters and cannot be read as industrial cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C53; calculation C62.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow quality is flattered by working capital and by the run-off of the finance book: nine-month 2026 operating cash flow was USD 348.21 million against USD 161.56 million a year earlier, helped by a smaller payables outflow and by a USD 87.50 million fall in finance receivables, so LTM operating cash flow of USD 569.91 million exceeds LTM reported EBITDA of USD 497.69 million. Receivable run-off is cash the business can use once, and it shrinks the financing revenue line, so the surplus over EBITDA is not a recurring cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C31; calculation C22.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was cash of USD 268.51 million plus stated remaining revolver capacity of USD 427.00 million, with USD 64 million of the cash at foreign subsidiaries, against a current portion of debt of USD 24.73 million and no final maturity before March 2029. Two springing tests tie the term loan and revolver to the bonds: if the 2029 notes are not redeemed by December 14, 2028 and liquidity is below their redemption amount plus USD 100 million, those facilities fall due on that day, and a similar test applies to the convertible notes before May 16, 2030. That definition is not supplied, so covenant and springing-test headroom is not calculable here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C46.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer deposits at The Pitney Bowes Bank of USD 647.95 million at September 30, 2026 are a non-debt funding float equal to 34.33% of carrying debt. They stood at USD 653.63 million at year-end 2025 and are repayable to depositors, and the annual report names significant withdrawals as a liquidity risk, so an outflow would have to be replaced by cash or debt; the deposits sit outside Total Debt and outside every ratio above, so those ratios understate claims on the group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C49; calculation C65.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the balance sheet date the issuer bought back shares for USD 11 million between October 1 and October 23, 2026, which would lift net leverage from 3.25x to 3.27x, and declared a dividend payable on December 8, 2026 whose total is not stated. U.S. pension lump-sum payments of USD 66 million were made from plan assets in October 2026 and a buy-out of the remaining plan is intended before year end; neither is stated as a company cash outflow, and none of these events is blended into the period figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C41; calculation C42.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer's own figures differ from the definitions used here in four places, and each is logged: it states only adjusted EBITDA, its income statement shows interest net of the amount allocated to cost of financing, its adjusted free cash flow adds back restructuring payments of USD 35.59 million in nine months, and from 2026 its adjusted measures exclude pension expense that earlier periods carry. The tender offer is a multi-figure event: USD 46 million of notes were redeemed at a discount for a gain of USD 5 million, while the year-to-date cash flow statement shows USD 402.03 million of principal payments, so gross repayment and net debt reduction are different figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C50; calculation C64.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an improving credit is that the improvement came from paydown financed by operating cash flow that benefited from finance-receivable run-off, while shareholder returns absorbed most of that cash and reported EBITDA fell year on year in the third quarter. A further buyback programme, a smaller receivable release or a weaker Presort quarter would reverse the move; sustained net leverage under 3.25x with returns below operating cash flow less capital expenditures would support it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C63; calculation C44.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the balance sheet date of September 30, 2026 the following events are flagged and kept out of the period figures: lump-sum pension payments of USD 66 million made from plan assets in October 2026 and an intended buy-out of the remaining U.S. plan before year end; share repurchases of USD 11 million from October 1 to October 23, 2026; and a dividend of USD 0.10 per share payable on December 8, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Amounts are USD thousands as the filings print them, and the financing cost adjustment is the only negative row.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ratios use EBITDA derived from reported lines because the issuer states none, and the debt includes borrowings that fund finance receivables.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest paid includes interest on the debt that funds finance receivables, and the year-to-date cash figures are the issuer's supplemental disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash includes USD 64 million held at foreign subsidiaries at 2026-09-30, and remaining facility capacity is not stated at the first two dates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ladder is drawn by final maturity at 2026-09-30 because the third-quarter report gives no repayment schedule by year, so the current portion of USD 24.730 million sits inside the term loan rows and no row is shown for 2026 to 2028; the annual report's schedule at 2025-12-31 still includes the 2027 notes repaid in the second quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The adjusted EBITDA of 2026 quarters excludes pension expense of the plans being terminated while 2025 quarters do not, so the year-on-year gain is overstated by that amount.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The stack omits USD 810 million of notes whose rank is not stated, so cumulative leverage above the secured loans is a floor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The bridge starts from derived reported EBITDA and ends at the issuer's adjusted EBITDA; the pension step of USD 23.125 million appears in 2026 only.

fields.value: - In the income statement, these cells are stated gaps and never zero: Other (income) expense for Q1 2026 (printed as a dash). They restrict nothing in the ratios, because every total and subtotal the ratios use is printed. Severity is Low; no action is needed for the ratios.

They restrict nothing in the ratios, because every total and subtotal the ratios use is printed. Severity is Low; no action is needed for the ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no adjusted EBITDA for full-year 2025, so adjusted leverage and adjusted cover are not calculable for any period and the adjusted rows of the calculation register say so. It restricts every adjusted-EBITDA ratio. Severity is Medium; the fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No unadjusted EBITDA is stated by the issuer, so EBITDA (Reported) is derived from income before taxes, total interest expense and depreciation and amortization for every period. It restricts how far the ratios can be compared with the issuer's own figures. Severity is Medium; no action closes it beyond the issuer stating it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt, cash, capital spending and liquidity are consolidated only, with no split between the finance operations and the industrial business, although the group holds finance receivables and customer deposits at the Bank. It restricts industrial leverage, matched-funding analysis and the meaning of consolidated cover. Severity is High; a split from the issuer would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The annual report supplied is the Form 10-K, while every 2026 filing and release cites a Form 10-K/A for the same year that is not supplied; the year-end 2025 balance sheet lines agree with the third-quarter comparative. It restricts confidence in FY2025 income statement and cash flow figures. Severity is Medium; supplying the Form 10-K/A would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Remaining revolver capacity is stated at 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30 only, and the amount of letters of credit at 2026-09-30 is not printed; the difference between facility size and stated capacity is USD 23 million at both dates after borrowings outstanding. It restricts the liquidity chart to two periods. Severity is Low; the letters of credit amount at each date would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The third-quarter report gives no repayment schedule by year, so the debt maturity chart is drawn by final maturity at 2026-09-30 and the term loan amortisation, stated only as a current portion of USD 24.73 million, sits inside the term loan rows. It restricts the near-term years, which carry no row because no instrument has a final maturity before March 2029. Severity is Medium; the amortisation schedules would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No source states the rank, security or guarantors of the notes due 2029, 2037 and 2043 or the guarantor list of the credit agreement; the debt stack therefore leaves out USD 810 million of notes and the instrument table marks their terms as not supplied; the guarantee wording of the convertible notes implies that some wholly owned U.S. subsidiaries guarantee the senior notes, but no source says which subsidiaries or which notes. It restricts cumulative leverage above the secured loans to a floor. Severity is Medium; the indentures would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Floors on the SOFR-based loans and scheduled amortisation of each instrument are not stated, so the instrument table carries them as not supplied. It restricts the interest sensitivity and the near-term repayment profile. Severity is Low; the credit agreement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The second-quarter report gives the term loan and revolver maturity as March 2031 while the third-quarter report gives May 2031 and describes the second-quarter extension as to May 2031; the later report is used and the earlier wording is logged. It restricts the exact month of the 2031 maturity. Severity is Low; the Fifth Amendment to the credit agreement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The cash flow statements of the quarterly reports are year-to-date, so no discrete second- or third-quarter cash flow is stated, and the 2025 depreciation and amortization of the quarters adds to 1 more than the nine-month statement figure by rounding; EBITDA for nine months 2025 follows the statement. It restricts discrete-quarter cash flow analysis. Severity is Low; no action is needed for the ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PITNEY BOWES INC /DE/ (issuer id pbi), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit snapshot. Scope: Business & governance, covering the business model, ownership and control, transactions and new debt, shareholder and management behaviour and governance risk, built from the seven supplied filings and releases and the source readiness analysis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors rest on a stable but slowly shrinking mail and shipping business with no controlling owner named in the filings and with shareholder returns running ahead of debt repayment, so protection comes from covenants and management's continued paydown, not owner support. In the first nine months of 2026 buybacks and dividends were USD 246.32 million against USD 107.78 million of debt principal repaid, and in 2025 they were USD 429.42 million against operating cash flow of USD 383.26 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation A09; calculation A10.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk is rated medium: the documents supplied show no sponsor fees, related-party payments or creditor-adverse transactions, but a board-led shift to buybacks, a new executive team and unexplained strategic review costs leave the direction of capital allocation to board discretion. The proxy statement and the executed debt documents are not supplied, so board independence, the large holders and the limits on distributions are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 99–100; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; Source readiness (CP-0).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two profit pools are moving in opposite directions, so group earnings are held up by SendTech cost cuts while Presort loses margin. SendTech adjusted segment EBIT rose 17.34% in the first nine months of 2026 on revenue that fell 1.06%, helped by lower selling, general and administrative expense and a USD 5 million tariff refund, and its margin reached 37.84%. Presort adjusted segment EBIT fell 26.19% as its margin dropped from 25.86% to 19.92% on lower volumes, price actions and higher transport and fuel costs. SendTech now supplies 79.41% of segment EBIT against 70.82% a year earlier, which concentrates creditor reliance on a business whose meter population and lease portfolio are shrinking.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation A02; calculation A04; calculation A05; calculation A06.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Both segments lean on the same postal system, so a rule, rate or volume shock would hit both profit pools together rather than diversify risk. The annual report says a significant portion of revenue depends on the USPS and other national posts, that postal authorities regulate and must approve many offerings, and that physical mail volumes are in continuing decline. The issuer describes Presort as the largest USPS workshare partner and the United States earned 84.27% of 2025 revenue. No client exceeded 10% of net sales in 2025 or 2024, which limits client concentration, but the business relies in places on single-source suppliers and on third-party transport.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The finance arm adds a shrinking asset base and a deposit float, so a quarter of operating cash flow is a run-off release that cannot be assumed to repeat. Net finance receivables fell 9.67% to USD 995.10 million between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30 as the lease portfolio shrank, with clients extending leases of existing equipment instead of buying new, and cash released from receivables supplied 25.13% of nine-month operating cash flow after 27.98% in 2025. The Pitney Bowes Bank held USD 647.95 million of customer deposits, 7.94% less than at the end of 2024, and the annual report names depositor withdrawals as a liquidity risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation A15; calculation A16.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control rests with a public board and its shareholders, not a sponsor, so creditors have no equity cure or sponsor support to count on and no sponsor fee leakage to price. Directors, large holders, related-party dealings and compensation are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that is not supplied, so board independence and the holders are not established. The filings do show that funds linked to the chief executive officer hold shares and adopted a trading arrangement in November 2025 covering up to 4.00% of shares outstanding, while buybacks cut the share count by 9.60% between January and October 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation A12; calculation A13.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Senior leadership is new and was drawn from the board, so the capital allocation record is short and the strategy is still being set. Three of the five executive officers have held office only since 2025 and each served as a director beforehand, the chief executive officer joined the board in May 2023 and was appointed in May 2025, and the annual report names leadership change as a continuity risk. Transaction and strategic review costs totalled USD 42.25 million from 2024 to September 2026 without any description of the review, so the chance of a leveraged transaction can be neither dismissed nor sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation A20; calculation A21.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns were set above what free cash flow supported in 2025 and still absorb most operating cash flow in 2026, so deleveraging is a board choice rather than a commitment. In 2025 returns of USD 429.42 million exceeded operating cash flow less capital expenditures by USD 112.44 million, net debt rose USD 258.17 million and cash fell USD 184.84 million, and part of the net proceeds of the 2025 convertible notes was used to repurchase shares in an amount the sources do not give. In 2026 returns are 2.29x debt principal repaid, the repurchase authorisation stands at USD 750 million with USD 165.91 million left, and the quarterly dividend is USD 0.10 per share.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; calculation A09; calculation A10; calculation A11; calculation A18.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ecommerce exit left a contingent claim and an impaired loan outside the debt figures, so legacy exposure is a liquidity risk the filings cannot size. A Pitney Bowes subsidiary kept 19% of the votes and all of the economic interest in the ecommerce subsidiary, which the issuer values at zero, and USD 8.00 million of the debtor-in-possession loan is fully reserved. The Kingsbridge and Trilogy claim is stated as USD 95 million in the annual report and as more than USD 100 million in the latest quarterly report; management expects no material adverse effect but the accrual is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation A17.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing in 2025 and 2026 moved debt toward secured bank loans and cleared near-term maturities, which helps liquidity but places holders of notes of unstated security behind a larger secured loan base. Term loans rose from 36.65% to 45.79% of debt principal, the notes due March 2027 were repaid from a term loan add-on, USD 150 million was added to the notes due March 2029, and no final maturity falls before March 2029. Maintenance covenants require interest coverage of at least 2.00x, secured net leverage of at most 3.00x and total net leverage of at most 4.75x in 2026, stepping down to 4.00x after 2028, and the term loan due 2031 and the revolver accelerate if liquidity is short of the 2029 notes plus USD 100 million before December 14, 2028 (and likewise for the convertible notes before May 16, 2030).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a medium risk reading is that creditors have been paid: debt principal fell USD 107.78 million in nine months, net debt fell USD 89.24 million after rising in 2025, a tender offer retired USD 46 million of notes at a discount, the margin on the 2032 term loan was cut by 75 bp, the revolver was raised to USD 450 million and no final maturity falls before March 2029. Buybacks in 2026 were covered by operating cash flow, and USD 165.91 million of authorisation remaining is small beside the debt outstanding. Evidence that would move the view toward low risk is a stated payout policy tied to net leverage, a proxy statement showing an independent board with no holder able to force a change, and disclosed covenant headroom. Evidence that would move it toward high risk is repurchases funded by revolver draws or new notes, a distribution that uses a covenant basket, an adverse ruling on the Kingsbridge claim or a leveraged transaction arising from the strategic review.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation A10; calculation A11; calculation A18.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling owner exists, the board's independence and the size of the large holdings are not established and could move the ownership and governance reading either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so the conclusion that creditors depend on covenants cannot be tested: the room to pay dividends and buy back shares, the collateral and the guarantors are known only from filing summaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating or market price is supplied, so the medium governance risk level has no external check and the market's view of the buyback and refinancing choices is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The purpose of the transaction and strategic review costs is not described, so the chance and size of a leveraged transaction cannot be assessed and event risk is left unquantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Kingsbridge and Trilogy accrual is not stated, so the claim cannot be sized against liquidity and management's view that the outcome will not be material is reported as management language only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The annual report supplied is the original Form 10-K while the 2026 filings cite a Form 10-K/A, so the 2025 comparisons of segment results and shareholder returns rest on figures that the amended filing may have changed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No material acquisition, sponsor buyout or change of control appears in the documents supplied; a USD 2.2 million acquisition in the first quarter of 2025 is the only one in the cash flow statements and is not described. The transactions that matter to creditors are the August 2024 ecommerce exit, the 2025 refinancing and convertible issue, and the 2026 note add-on, term loan extension and tender offer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In August 2024 the issuer sold 81% of the voting interests of its ecommerce logistics subsidiary to an affiliate of Hilco Commercial Industrial for de minimis consideration and kept 19% of the votes and all of the economic interest; the subsidiary then filed for Chapter 11 and its liquidation plan was confirmed on November 25, 2024. The issuer funded USD 28 million of debtor-in-possession financing, USD 20 million has been repaid and USD 8.00 million is fully reserved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In the first quarter of 2025 the issuer redeemed the remaining notes due March 2028 at a loss of USD 17 million and signed a new senior secured credit agreement with a revolver of USD 265 million (later USD 400 million), a USD 160 million term loan due 2028 and a USD 615 million term loan due 2032, recording a further loss of USD 8 million on the refinancing. In August 2025 it issued USD 230 million of 1.50% convertible senior notes due 2030 whose net proceeds of USD 221 million paid for a capped call (premium USD 24.70 million), share repurchases and general purposes, in amounts the sources do not split.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In 2026 the issuer added USD 150 million to its notes due March 2029, raised the revolver from USD 400 million to USD 450 million, borrowed USD 150 million more under its term loan and extended that loan to May 2031 to repay the notes due March 2027, tendered USD 46 million of its notes due 2037 and 2043 at a discount for a gain of USD 5 million, and cut the margin on the 2032 term loan by 75 bp. No final maturity now falls before March 2029, but the term loan due 2031 and the revolver accelerate if liquidity is below the cost of redeeming the 2029 notes plus USD 100 million before December 14, 2028, with a matching test for the convertible notes before May 16, 2030.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the 2026-09-30 balance sheet date the issuer repurchased shares for USD 11 million between October 1 and October 23, 2026, paid USD 66 million of pension lump sums from plan assets in October 2026 and the board approved a quarterly dividend of USD 0.10 per share payable on December 8, 2026. These subsequent events are kept out of the period figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PITNEY BOWES INC /DE/ (issuer id pbi), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit snapshot. Scope: Fundamental credit, the integrated credit view built from Source readiness, Financial foundation, Business & governance and the seven supplied filings and releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit quality is average: a cash-generative but slowly shrinking mail business has cut net leverage to 3.25x, or 3.27x pro forma for October repurchases, yet creditors depend on a running-off finance book and on a board that spends most free cash flow on shareholders. Cash flow before the finance receivable release covered buybacks and dividends only 1.05x over the last twelve months, leaving USD 17.56 million for debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F01; calculation F02; calculation F06; calculation F07.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity of USD 695.51 million and no final maturity before March 2029 give time, but 82.59% of principal falls due from 2029 to 2032 and the primary downside is faster mail erosion while buybacks continue. The dividend payable on December 8, 2026 is not reflected in the pro forma figure because its total is not stated, and pro forma liquidity is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 1; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F03; calculation F04; calculation F02.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is average and weakening: two segments that both depend on the postal system earn a high margin on a base that is shrinking. Total revenue fell 6.61% in 2025 and 2.11% in the first nine months of 2026, and the shrinkage is steady rather than sudden. SendTech earns an adjusted EBIT margin of 37.84%, with services at 45.48% of its revenue and USD 624.43 million of contracted future performance obligations, but 38.22% of its revenue is lease and financing income from a shrinking book, and Presort lost 5.94 percentage points of margin and 26.19% of adjusted EBIT on a 4.18% revenue fall, an operating leverage of 6.27x. A decline in mail volumes therefore cuts earnings faster than revenue in the segment that has a fixed processing and transport network.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F10; calculation F13; calculation F15; calculation F19.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is real but flattered, so creditors should size debt service on operating cash flow before the finance receivable release. Operating cash flow over the last twelve months was USD 569.91 million, 114.51% of EBITDA (Reported), but without USD 100.00 million released from a shrinking finance receivable book it was 94.42%, and 79.49% of the USD 186.66 million nine-month rise came from a smaller outflow on payables and accruals. Operating cash flow before the release, less capital expenditures of USD 65.29 million, was USD 404.62 million, inside the range of the issuer's 2026 adjusted free cash flow guidance, USD 380 million to USD 420 million, which is defined differently.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 67; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F06; calculation F08; calculation F09.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has improved by 0.52x since year-end 2025 but not on a growing earnings base, so further gains depend on cash that the board can redirect. Net debt to EBITDA (Reported) fell from 3.77x at year-end 2025 to 3.25x at 2026-09-30, or 3.27x pro forma for the USD 11 million of repurchases to October 23, 2026; the effect of the dividend payable on December 8, 2026 is not established because its total is not stated, and pro forma cash is not established. Of the fall, 0.32x came from higher EBITDA and 0.20x from lower net debt, but the EBITDA gain follows losses of USD 45.68 million on foreign exchange and debt activities in nine months 2025 and gains of USD 8.77 million in 2026, and last-twelve-month EBITDA has slipped from USD 503.26 million at 2026-06-30 to USD 497.69 million. The issuer's adjusted EBITDA rose 4.49% to USD 432.41 million in nine months only because USD 23.13 million of pension expense is excluded from 2026 and not from 2025; on the 2025 definition it fell 1.10%. EBITDA covered cash interest 3.65x, and a 10% fall in EBITDA at constant net debt would lift net leverage to 3.61x, a 20% fall to 4.07x. The computed 3.25x sits below the 4.75x total net leverage covenant level for 2026 but is not covenant headroom, because the agreement's definitions are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 9; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F01; calculation F02; calculation F12; calculation F16; calculation F20.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for the next two years but the maturity wall is concentrated and conditional, so refinancing is the central test after 2028. Cash plus remaining revolver capacity was USD 695.51 million at 2026-09-30 against a current portion of debt of USD 24.73 million (pro forma liquidity is not established), yet 82.59% of principal matures between 2029 and 2032 and two springing tests accelerate the 2031 term loan and the revolver if liquidity is below the redemption amount of the 2029 notes plus USD 100 million, a test amount of USD 576.00 million, before December 14, 2028, with a matching test of USD 330.00 million for the convertible notes before May 16, 2030. The liquidity definition sits in an agreement that is not supplied, so headroom is not calculable. Term loans are 45.79% of principal at floating rates, so a 100 bp move changes annual interest by USD 8.78 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F03; calculation F04; calculation F05.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the swing factor because shareholder returns, not debt service, set the pace of deleveraging. Returns of USD 387.07 million over the last twelve months were 95.66% of operating cash flow less capital expenditures before the release, and in 2025 returns of USD 429.42 million exceeded operating cash flow of USD 383.26 million; in the first nine months of 2026 returns were 2.29x the USD 107.78 million of debt principal repaid, with USD 165.91 million of repurchase authorisation left. The board can cut returns at any time and the covenants cap leverage, but the baskets that limit distributions are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F07; calculation F14.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figures and missing documents limit confidence more than any single ratio. Customer deposits at the Pitney Bowes Bank were USD 647.95 million at 2026-09-30 and the issuer names depositor withdrawals as a liquidity risk, a claim larger than cash, the Kingsbridge and Trilogy suit seeks more than USD 100 million with no accrual stated, and the pension buy-out is not costed. Debt and cash are reported for the whole group, so industrial leverage and the finance book's matched funding cannot be separated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F15.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside is faster erosion of the mail base while the finance book stops releasing cash and buybacks continue, and its first visible sign would be a Presort quarter with less volume than the second quarter of 2026 or a falling receivable release. The guidance implies fourth-quarter adjusted EBIT of USD 89.65 million to USD 109.65 million, 3.74% to 21.30% below the third quarter, and adjusted free cash flow of USD 41.24 million to USD 81.24 million, so the guidance implies that part of the third-quarter cash benefit, which the issuer attributes to new client prepayments after a competitor's exit, does not repeat.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_q22026earningspressrelea.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation F11.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better credit is that leverage fell and cover rose without a distress event: net debt to EBITDA (Reported) fell from 3.77x to 3.25x, or 3.27x pro forma for the October repurchases with the dividend effect not established, cover rose from 3.19x to 3.65x, Presort volume returned to growth of 4% in the third quarter after a competitor's exit, 2026 revenue guidance was raised at the low end to USD 1,830 million to USD 1,860 million, and debt was refinanced with no final maturity before 2029 and a 75 bp lower margin on the largest loan. If operating cash flow before the release stays near USD 404.62 million while returns are held below it, net debt could fall faster than the base case and the credit would merit a stronger assessment. The case for a weaker credit wins if the Presort margin keeps falling, if the finance book's release fades, or if buybacks are funded from the revolver, because returns already take 95.66% of cash flow before the release; covenant headroom on the agreement's own definitions, a stated payout policy and the proxy statement are the evidence that would settle the question.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-05_q12026earningspressrelea.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F01; calculation F06; calculation F07.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant definitions and compliance figures are not supplied, so the conclusion that leverage sits below the covenant levels is an indication on reported EBITDA derived from the statements and not a measured headroom; a definition with fewer add-backs or tighter cash netting could narrow it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt, cash and cash flow are consolidated with the finance operations, so the leverage and cover conclusions cannot be restated for the industrial business and could be better or worse on that basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Only issuer-adjusted EBITDA for 2026 quarters is supplied and none for full-year 2025, so the conclusion on earnings direction rests on EBITDA (Reported) and the adjusted-basis comparison cannot be drawn for the last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The security of the 2029, 2037 and 2043 notes and the names of their guarantors are not stated, so the conclusion that secured bank debt is rising ahead of notes cannot be turned into a priority ranking.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No ratings, market prices or peer financials are supplied, so the business profile is judged on the issuer's own trend and not against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The outlook beyond the 2026 guidance is qualitative because no multi-year forecast is supplied, so the medium-term conclusion on deleveraging rests on the structure of cash flows and not on a projection.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A contracted, high-margin SendTech base supports debt service, because SendTech future performance obligations are USD 624.43 million, services are 45.48% of its revenue and its adjusted EBIT margin is 37.84%, so a large part of cash flow is visible several quarters ahead and survives a weak equipment year, although 38.22% of its revenue is lease and financing income from a shrinking book.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F15; calculation F19.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale in a regulated niche supports Presort cash flow, because the issuer describes itself as the largest USPS workshare partner with a national processing network and volume grew 4% in the third quarter, so scale supports volume retention and client wins, although the same dependence on the postal service is also the main risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Falling leverage and rising cover support creditors, because net debt to EBITDA (Reported) fell to 3.25x, or 3.27x pro forma for the October repurchases with the dividend effect not established, and cover rose to 3.65x, so the issuer could absorb a 10% EBITDA fall and still sit at 3.61x on this measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F01; calculation F02; calculation F12.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinanced liquidity and a late first maturity support the near term, because cash plus remaining revolver capacity is USD 695.51 million, pro forma liquidity is not established, no final maturity falls before March 2029 and the margin on the 2032 term loan was cut by 75 bp, so refinancing risk does not arise before the springing-test date in December 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 1; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F03.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Low capital intensity and completed restructuring support conversion, because capital expenditures are 3.51% of revenue and the 2025 plan that removed about 550 positions finished in the second quarter of 2026, so a large share of EBITDA reaches cash before interest and returns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Structural decline of the mail base constrains creditors, because the meter population and the mailing install base are eroding, Presort volume fell in the first half of 2026 before growing 4% in the third quarter, total revenue fell 6.61% in 2025 and Presort adjusted EBIT fell 26.19% on a 4.18% revenue fall, so earnings are exposed to operating leverage that a lender cannot hedge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F10; calculation F13.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow quality constrains creditors, because operating cash flow of USD 569.91 million includes USD 100.00 million released from finance receivables and a payables swing worth 79.49% of the nine-month rise, so the surplus over EBITDA is not a recurring cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F06; calculation F09.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns constrain deleveraging, because buybacks and dividends took 95.66% of cash flow before the release over the last twelve months and exceeded operating cash flow less capital expenditures in 2025, so the board, not the lenders, decides how fast debt falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F07; calculation F14.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Maturity concentration and conditionality constrain refinancing, because 82.59% of principal matures from 2029 to 2032, two springing tests tie the 2031 term loan and the revolver to liquidity, and floating-rate term loans are 45.79% of principal against 37% a year earlier, so a weak 2028 would narrow the refinancing window and raise interest cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F04; calculation F05.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside debt and missing documents constrain confidence, because Bank deposits of USD 647.95 million, a lawsuit seeking more than USD 100 million without a stated accrual and an uncosted pension buy-out sit outside the debt figures, and the executed credit agreement and the proxy statement are not supplied, so headroom and governance cannot be verified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation F15; calculation F16.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer provides shipping and mailing technology, mail sortation and equipment financing to clients that include more than nine in ten of the Fortune 500, and earns its cash flow from long-lived service, maintenance, subscription and sortation contracts and from a finance book. That model supports debt service while installed equipment stays in use, but it weakens as physical mail volumes and meter populations fall, because services and supplies revenue follow the installed base and the finance book follows new equipment placements. Contract terms of one to five years with annual renewals give visibility, and no client exceeded 10% of net sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F15.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is public with no sponsor named, so there is no equity cure, no fee leakage and no sponsor behaviour to assess; the board decides distributions, the leadership team is new, and the 2024 sale of the ecommerce business left a retained economic interest valued at zero and legal claims. The consequence is that financial policy rests on board discretion and covenants, and that group structure beyond the Bank and the ecommerce debtors is not shown by the documents supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable in the services and sortation lines but declining in the installed base: SendTech services are flat, products and financing revenue fall as clients extend leases instead of buying equipment and the lease portfolio shrinks, and Presort revenue fell 4.18% on volume and price actions. Pricing power is limited by competition from online shipping platforms and regional sortation providers and by postal rules, although Presort won new clients in the third quarter after a competitor left the market. Revenue is therefore recurring, regulated and structurally declining at a slow pace, which supports cash flow for several years but not growth in debt capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F15.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are largely fixed in the Presort network and flexible in SendTech: SendTech cut selling, general and administrative expense by USD 45 million in nine months and received a USD 5 million tariff refund, while Presort transport and fuel costs rose USD 15 million, so SendTech margin gains are finite and partly one-off and Presort margins are exposed to freight cost inflation and volume loss. Capital expenditures are 3.51% of revenue and the 2025 restructuring plan is complete, so further cost cuts need new actions and capex cannot be cut much further.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_q22026earningspressrelea.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation F10.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is high but not clean: operating cash flow less capital expenditures was 101.39% of EBITDA (Reported) over the last twelve months, and operating cash flow alone was 94.42% once the finance receivable release is removed, with restructuring payments, cash interest and cash taxes already deducted in operating cash flow. Cash interest paid of USD 136.27 million is 27.38% of EBITDA, so interest absorbs roughly a quarter of operating earnings before returns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F06; calculation F08.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is moderate and pressures price at the margin, because SendTech competes with other mail equipment providers and online shipping platforms and its finance arm competes with banks and leasing companies, while Presort faces regional providers and large mailers that can sort in-house; the consequence is price actions at Presort and a need to keep equipment sales and leases competitive. The threat of new entrants is low in regulated meter and sortation lines because postal authorities must approve many new offerings, but high in digital shipping where platforms negotiate carrier rates, which limits growth. The threat of substitutes is the central risk because electronic communication replaces physical mail, and buyer power is meaningful at Presort, where client losses in the first half of 2025 cut volume; supplier power is meaningful through single-source suppliers and through the postal service as regulator and counterparty.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_q12026earningspressrelea.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulatory and economic factors are material to credit: postal rules and rates, bank regulation of the Utah industrial bank, tariffs on SendTech components (offset by a refund in 2026) and the level of interest rates all change cash flow or funding cost, so floating-rate term loans of USD 878.48 million expose annual interest to USD 8.78 million for each 100 bp. Social and technological shifts are the same substitution risk already described.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are a lasting Presort volume recovery after a competitor's exit and further repayment from the finance book's run-off. Threats that could weaken it are an adverse postal rule or rate change, faster mail decline, a leveraged transaction arising from the strategic review and an adverse outcome in the Kingsbridge and Trilogy suit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are average and competitive advantage is average: revenue of USD 1,862.72 million over the last twelve months and the largest USPS workshare network give relevance and shock absorption, but the advantage is a position in a shrinking market rather than a moat, so it supports stability and not growth. Business diversification is weak, because both segments and the finance book depend on physical mail and the postal service, and 84.27% of 2025 revenue is earned in the United States.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 83; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F10; calculation F15.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost and capex flexibility is average and margin stability is average: capital expenditures are small and the restructuring is finished, and group adjusted EBIT rose 9.42% in nine months of 2026, but only 2.40% on the 2025 definition that keeps pension expense, SendTech gains came from cost cuts and one-off items and Presort margins fell, so margins depend on actions that cannot be repeated each year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation F10; calculation F15; calculation F20.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow stability is average: cash conversion is high at 101.39% of EBITDA, but USD 100.00 million of release and a payables swing flatter it, and returns absorb 95.66% of what remains, so free cash flow is large but not stable enough to be treated as available for debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F06; calculation F07; calculation F09.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: the issuer refinanced in 2025 and 2026, added USD 150 million to the 2029 notes and extended a term loan, and no maturity falls before March 2029, but 82.59% of principal matures from 2029 to 2032, security shifted toward bank loans and no rating is supplied. Liquidity is average: cash plus remaining revolver capacity of USD 695.51 million (pro forma liquidity is not established) far exceeds the near-term current debt, but access to the revolver depends on covenants whose definitions are not supplied and Bank deposits of USD 647.95 million are a claim on the group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F03; calculation F04.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy and governance are average: no related-party leakage or sponsor fee appears and covenants are maintained, but returns exceed debt repayment, the leadership team is new and board independence is not established, which matches a medium governance risk level and leaves the assessment open to change when the proxy statement and executed documents are available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the issuer guides to 2026 revenue of USD 1,830 million to USD 1,860 million, adjusted EBIT of USD 450 million to USD 470 million and adjusted free cash flow of USD 380 million to USD 420 million, which implies a weaker fourth quarter than the third, and total net leverage covenant levels step down from 4.75x in 2026 to 4.50x in 2027 and 4.25x in 2028. The tailwinds are cost reductions already taken, a lower margin on the 2032 term loan, Presort client wins and the removal of pension volatility; the headwinds are the finance book run-off, higher transport costs, new equipment sales deferred by lease extensions and the expiry of one-off benefits. The net effect is stable earnings and continued paydown only if returns stay below free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991q32026earningspress.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation F11.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the 2029 notes, the 2030 convertible notes and the 2031 and 2032 term loans mature in close order, the springing tests bring the 2029 refinancing forward to December 2028, and mail volumes and the meter base keep eroding, so the sector headwind compounds while the finance book shrinks; deleveraging before 2028 is the main protection against a refinancing in a weaker earnings base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; Financial foundation (CP-1).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside starts with a faster fall in physical mail volumes or an adverse postal rule, which first breaks the Presort network economics because its margin fell 5.94 percentage points on a 4.18% revenue fall, and then erodes SendTech services and supplies revenue as the meter base shrinks. EBITDA falls and the finance book releases less cash, so operating cash flow loses part of the USD 100.00 million release and of the payables benefit; if buybacks and dividends continue at the last-twelve-month rate of USD 387.07 million, net debt stops falling and net leverage rises, to 3.61x after a 10% EBITDA fall and 4.07x after 20% at constant net debt. Rising leverage tightens the stepped-down total net leverage covenant and the revolver, and the springing tests make a refinancing of the 2029 notes necessary by December 2028 unless liquidity exceeds the notes plus USD 100 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation F03; calculation F06; calculation F07; calculation F12; calculation F13.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management has levers: it can stop buybacks and dividends, which are discretionary and were USD 246.32 million in nine months, let the finance book run off, defer restructuring and use the revolver, and the debt maturities leave time to act. On the figures available, resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 if returns are cut at the first signal, but not if returns are held while volumes fall; the observable triggers are a Presort quarter with less volume than the second quarter of 2026, a lower receivable release, revolver use at a quarter end and repurchases above cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F14.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Pitney Bowes presents an adequate business profile supported by contracted SendTech services, a national Presort network and low capital intensity, but credit quality is constrained by a structurally shrinking mail base, a finance-book release that flatters cash flow and shareholder returns that absorb most free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because operating cash flow before the release was USD 404.62 million after capital expenditures, though it is not stable. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on deleveraging before December 2028, on covenant headroom that is not calculable and on lender appetite for notes whose security is not stated. The primary downside path is faster mail erosion with continuing buybacks. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, the proxy statement, an industrial-versus-finance split and the Form 10-K/A. Top risk: shareholder returns and mail erosion absorbing the cash that would repay the 2029 notes.
